sentences: A Sentinel-1D pair spanning the event lost coherence inside an independently mapped detachment while the nearby control ring gained coherence.
After a control-calibrated threshold and four-pixel minimum area, 158 of 307 target pixels were flagged, versus 1225 false alarms among 30161 control pixels.
The pattern is retrospective evidence of localized surface change, not proof of a precursor, cause, displacement, or warning capability.
NISAR L-band median coherence fell from 0.219 in the quiet pair to 0.102 in the event pair, while the exploratory control changed only from 0.862 to 0.846.
Only 9 of 528 source pixels retained connected unwrapped phase in the event pair.
The satellite saw decorrelation, but the data do not support a displacement map or a claim that the slope was moving beforehand.
The first Sentinel-1D image used here was acquired 2.395 days after the event.
Its CMR insertion was 3.254 days after the event, while the matching OPERA RTC product was inserted about 46.379 days after the event in this archive snapshot.
These are retrospective acquisition and archive delays, not warning time or operational delivery guarantees.
